text:
Alice: Heads-up, saw a couple of failed Pod scheduling events in eu-west-2 last night. Looks like GPU node pools hit fragmentation when autoscaler tried to pack time-slice workloads into MIG-configured nodes.
Ben: Seen similar in ap-south — ENI limits + burst provisioning caused attach errors. Not pure MIG problem, network quotas biting us.
Carla: Quick summary of what happened: autoscaler requested 4 nodes, cloud returned 4 large instances with different MIG partitioning than our packing heuristic expected, pods couldn't land on the returned nodes -> backoff -> more autoscaler churn.
Diego: Oof. Any logs?
Alice: Pasted relevant event snippets below:
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  pod/my-inference-xyz  0/12 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 4 node(s) had taint {dedicated=gpu:NoSchedule}, 2 failed attach volume "eni-attach".
Autoscaler: scaleUp computed 4, launched 4, 2 timed out for binding due to attach errors
```
Ben: The attach errors correlate with ENI saturation on those instance types in ap-south. We need region-aware instance selection or smaller instance families there.
Eva: For eu-west we also saw mismatch because some nodepools are provisioned as MIG 7g.1 and others as MIG 3g.2 — our scheduler predicate for packing assumes a common MIG shape.
Carla: Proposed mitigation (short-term): 1) Create region-specific compact nodepools that enforce a single MIG profile. 2) Autoscaler scaling-window tweaks to avoid simultaneous conflicting launches. 3) Add an ENI headroom buffer in ap-south.
Diego: Agree. Also let's add a fallback to time-sliced nodes for low-latency bursts so small jobs can go to time-slice pools instead of waiting for a new MIG-conforming node.
infra-sre: Note: switching between MIG<->timeslice requires driver restart on node in some kernels; expect ~90s additional node init.
Ben: Can we express the nodepool config as annotations to make autoscaler prefer certain pools? Example suggestion:
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"
    autoscaler.k8s.aws/priority: "high"
spec:
  taints:
  - key: "gpu-shape"
    value: "7g.1"
    effect: NoSchedule
```
Carla: I'd rather use labels for bin-packing: node.kubernetes.io/gpu-profile=7g.1 and have pod affinity to prefer that profile. Then autoscaler can scale specific pools.
Alice: For cost tradeoffs — time-slicing increases utilization but raises tail latency and complexity; MIG reduces tail but increases fragmentation. We should map workloads: high qps interactive -> time-slice pool, long batched -> MIG-dedicated.
Eva: Also flagging spot behavior: when spot preemption occurs, MIG nodes can evict many pods at once. Time-slice may distribute risk across more nodes.
Diego: Ops playbook idea: when we expect a surge (marketing demo / flash test), run this sequence:
- Lock autoscaler down (scale-down disabled + scale-up target set)
- Pre-warm a small dedicated-MIG pool in target region (3 nodes, MIG 7g.1)
- Pre-warm a time-slice pool for interactive traffic (to absorb small requests)
- Set k8s-bot alert thresholds for attach failures and ENI saturation
- After surge, drain time-slice pool first, then scale-down MIG pool
Carla: We should codify that into a runbook and a terraform module to create the two nodepools with appropriate tags. I can draft a module.
k8s-bot: Cluster autoscaler: scaled up 3 nodes in eu-west-2 (nodepool=prewarm-mig-7g1).
Alice: Thanks — can someone create the prewarm nodepool in eu-west-2 and ap-south for a 48h window? Make it opt-in via infra-prewarm tag so billing is visible.
Ben: I'll spin up ap-south prewarm but using smaller instance family to avoid ENI constraints (g5.xlarge-ish).
Diego: I'll add an autoscaler policy tweak config to the PR: increase max-node-provision-time and add backoff to avoid tight launch loops.
Eva: Also adding monitoring: per-pool GPU utilization, per-node ENI usage, and a fragmentation metric (percent nodes with >25% gpu leftover).
Carla: Example fragment metric query (rough):
```
(sum by(node) (gpu_total - gpu_allocated) > 0) / count(nodes) * 100
```
Alice: Great. Action items: Ben create ap-south prewarm (due +3h), Carla draft terraform module (+1d), Diego autoscaler PR (+8h), Eva monitoring dashboards (+1d). I'll coordinate postmortem notes.
infra-sre: FYI: we should test node restart impact when switching MIG/time-slice in staging kernel 5.15 vs 5.19. Some customers using legacy drivers might be affected.
Ben: pinged @cloud-quotas to request temporary ENI increases in ap-south for the next 72h during the prewarm test.
Alice: Thanks team :thumbsup: We'll reconvene after the prewarm test and iterate on the runbook.
Carla: Adding doc link to the runbook draft when ready.
Diego: If anyone wants to simulate fragmentation locally, I have a script that creates mixed-size deployment requests to force the autoscaler into different shapes — I'll drop it in #eng-infra later.
Eva: Nice. Also, can we add an A/B to route a small % of traffic to time-slice pool to validate latencies before wide switch?
Alice: Yes — canary % = 5% for 24h.
Ben: Starting prewarm in 10m.
k8s-bot: Event: node/prewarm-mig-1 is Ready (ip=10.20.30.5)
